title: Hearing the Voice of the Lord: Principles and Patterns of Personal Revelation
author: Gerald N. Lund
target_audience: Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS/Mormon)
Individuals desiring to improve prayer and spiritual communication
core_themes: Learning the principles and patterns by which God communicates with individuals
Distinguishing between God's voice, personal thoughts, and other influences
primary_purpose: To teach readers how to recognize, understand, and respond to personal revelation and guidance from God, drawing upon scriptural teachings, prophetic counsel, and practical application for daily spiritual living.

structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters focusing on distinct principles of revelation, supported by scripture, prophetic quotations, and real-life examples
features: Scripture references from the Bible, Book of Mormon, and other LDS scripture
Stories from Church history and personal experiences

key_concepts_lessons: God desires to communicate with His children personally.
Revelation comes in many forms, not always as dramatic or audible voices.
Recognizing spiritual impressions requires practice and spiritual sensitivity.
There are consistent patterns and principles through which the Lord communicates.
Patience, faith, and obedience are key to receiving and acting on revelation.
The Holy Ghost plays a central role as the agent of divine communication.
notable_features: Focus on LDS doctrine and teachings regarding revelation
Extensive use of real-life stories and scriptural case studies
Step-by-step guidance for recognizing and acting upon revelation
Frequently used in LDS faith-promoting classes and discussions
cultural_historical_context: Written by a well-known LDS author and former Church leader, the book addresses a cornerstone concept in Latter-day Saint theology—that God speaks to individuals. Published during a period of increasing emphasis within the LDS community on personal spiritual experience and lay ministry.
reception_impact: Popular within LDS circles as an accessible, foundational text on personal revelation
Recommended for youth, adults, and new converts seeking to cultivate spiritual listening
Praised for blending doctrinal rigor with practical, everyday application
Sometimes noted as most valuable for those within the LDS tradition, given its doctrinal specificity
comparable_titles: The Holy Ghost by Joseph Fielding McConkie
Promptings of the Spirit by Richard G. Scott
Drawing on the Powers of Heaven by Grant Von Harrison
